## What monetary thresholds should the tailored severity categories use?

`DQ-002` · reversibility **revisit** · gate G0 · asked 2026-11-11

Table I uses $10M / $1M / $100K. For a simulation-and-bench demonstrator that would put **every equipment loss in Negligible**. The proposal keeps the injury and environmental criteria and scales money by 1/100. 4.3.3d requires tailored definitions to be derived from Table I and formally approved.

| Option | What it does and costs |
|---|---|
| **Scale by 1/100 ($100K / $10K / $1K)** (recommended) | Equipment damage registers at a sensible level. Injury criteria unchanged. |
| Keep Table I values | No tailoring to justify; equipment losses all rate Negligible. |
| Drop the monetary criterion | Rate on injury and environment only; loses the equipment-damage dimension. |

Blocks: SUS-RISKDEF-001 approval, every hazard risk assessment

Sources: standards/tailoring/mil-std-882e.yaml, MIL-STD-882E Table I, 4.3.3d

## What exposure basis should the probability levels use?

`DQ-003` · reversibility **easy** · gate G0 · asked 2026-11-11

4.3.3e requires numerical probability definitions to be documented. The proposal applies the Table A-II bands per item over a planned demonstrator life of **500 walker hours, 2,000 docking cycles and 200 UAV flight hours**, with one walker and two UAVs. These numbers are placeholders until the test programme exists.

| Option | What it does and costs |
|---|---|
| **Use the proposed item life** (recommended) | Lets PHA (Task 202) start now; revisit at G2. |
| Per operating hour | Simpler to compare across subsystems; less intuitive for docking-cycle hazards. |
| Wait for the test programme | Probabilities stay qualitative until G2. |

Blocks: SUS-RISKDEF-001 approval

Sources: standards/tailoring/mil-std-882e.yaml, MIL-STD-882E 4.3.3e, Appendix A Table A-II

## Who holds each risk-acceptance role, and is the proposed authority mapping right?

`DQ-004` · reversibility **revisit** · gate G4 · asked 2026-11-11

The proposal: High by a Program Executive, Serious by the Program Lead, Medium by the Chief Engineer, Low by the Safety Lead; a Test Operations representative concurs on High and Serious (4.3.7). All roles are **simulated**. Rule R13 now requires a named human in the right role on a review record before any risk is accepted, so no acceptance can happen until these roles are filled.

| Option | What it does and costs |
|---|---|
| **You hold PE, PL and CE; name a separate user representative** (recommended) | Quickest; the review records show one person in several roles. |
| Name a different person for each role | More independence; needs volunteers. |
| Change the mapping | For example, the Safety Lead accepts Medium as well as Low. |

Blocks: any risk acceptance, EVT-BENCH-001

Sources: standards/tailoring/mil-std-882e.yaml, MIL-STD-882E 4.3.7

## Should a passing PDaC validation be required before merging to main?

`DQ-005` · reversibility **easy** · gate G0 · asked 2026-11-11

The workflow "PDaC / MIL-STD-882E validation" runs on every pull request, but **nothing stops a merge when it fails**. Making it a required check is a repository setting only you can change.

| Option | What it does and costs |
|---|---|
| **Make it a required status check** (recommended) | Records on main always validate. A broken rule blocks merging until fixed. |
| Keep it advisory | Faster merges; drift can reach main. |

Sources: .github/workflows/pdac-validate.yml

## What power and actuation architecture is the baseline for analysis?

`DQ-006` · reversibility **hard** · gate G2 · asked 2026-11-11

The records disagree. README.md and the seeded hazards assume **hydraulic actuation**. The wiki architecture page assumes a **series-hybrid engine-generator with battery and electric or electrohydraulic joints**. Trade study TS-001 covers actuation but not the power source. The power sub-elements and IF-002/IF-003 are marked candidate until this is decided. The choice changes hazards (stored hydraulic energy vs fuel, battery thermal runaway) and the simulation plant.

| Option | What it does and costs |
|---|---|
| **Analyse both until TS-001 closes** (recommended) | Keep hydraulic and hybrid-electric as named alternatives; hazards tagged per alternative. More analysis now, no rework later. |
| Centralised hydraulic | Matches the README and current hazards; the sim plant models a hydraulic power unit. |
| Series-hybrid electric or electrohydraulic | Matches the wiki architecture page; adds fuel and battery hazards, removes most stored-pressure hazards. |

Blocks: SUS-M1-PWR sub-elements, IF-002, IF-003, sim plant model

Sources: README.md, docs/wiki/SUS-M1-Architecture-and-Boundaries.md, concept/trade-studies.md, framework/liondriver-port-plan.md

## What should the UAV do when it loses the link to the integration manager?

`DQ-008` · reversibility **easy** · gate G2 · asked 2026-11-11

In PX4 SITL (sim/results/uav/summary.md), return-to-launch on link loss **flies the aircraft back to the dock and descends 1.9 m from the pilot station**, inside the 3 m keep-out, with no recovery permit (SU-01). If the walker has moved, it lands 20 m away where the dock used to be (SU-02). Land-in-place keeps it 48 m clear (SU-03). The interface contract requires a defined, analysed contingency and an explicit permit for recovery.

| Option | What it does and costs |
|---|---|
| **Hold briefly, then land in place (NAV_DLL_ACT = Land)** (recommended) | Keeps the aircraft away from people at the walker; the UAV must be recovered by hand. Proven clear in SU-03. |
| Return to a rally point away from the walker | Keeps the aircraft recoverable; needs rally points kept up to date as the walker moves, and a permit before the final approach. More work in the integration manager. |
| Return to the dock (PX4 default return) | Recovers the aircraft automatically, but breaches the pilot keep-out in SU-01 and lands at a stale home in SU-02. |

Blocks: PX4 parameter baseline for SUS-A1, HAZ-INT-001 mitigation M4

Sources: sim/results/uav/summary.md, integrations/px4/interface-contract.md, safety/hazards/HAZ-INT-001.yaml
